newsitem.title: SPAIN: Baron de Ley share offer 20 times oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Baron de Ley share offer 20 times oversubscribed.

text.p: Spanish wine producer Baron de Ley said on Friday its initial public offer had been 20 times oversubscribed.
At the close of the period allotted to request shares, demand had reached 100 million shares compared with the initial offer of 4.8 million shares, Baron de Ley said in a statement.

"According to provisional data, national and international institutional investors have put in requests to buy shares equivalent to 200 billion pesetas, which implies the offer was 20 times oversubscribed," Baron de Ley said.
The oversubscription was equally divided between the national and international tranches. There is no retail tranche.
The domestic tranche accounts for 2.16 million shares or 45 percent of the offer, while the international tranche comprises 2.64 million shares, or 55 percent of the offer.
Friday was the final day for the request of shares. The final price of the share will be announced on Monday, and will be in a range between 1,950 and 2,250 pesetas per share.
Baron de Ley's shares will begin to trade on Wednesday.
The group is selling up to 74.6 percent of its capital or 5,407,860 shares including the "green shoe."
